stem: The four agent failure classes are…
options: Loops/stalls, runaway spend, goal drift, compounding error
explanation: Each exists because there is a loop; each has a code-shaped guardrail.

options: The same call with the same arguments, again - a model that did not get what it wanted just retries
explanation: Detect exact repeats; inject 'already tried; result was X' or stop.

stem: 'No new information in the window' catches…
options: Stalls that vary their calls slightly - progress means a (tool, args) pair not seen before
explanation: Weaker loops repeat with variations; freshness is the test.

options: An agent busy and succeeding at every call - on work irrelevant to the goal
explanation: Activity is not progress; the goal-relevance of the recent window is the cheap proxy.

stem: Budgets remain essential even with detectors because…
options: Novel failure shapes will slip pattern detectors; the cap bounds damage regardless
36% chance every step was right - and a wrong mid-trace fact poisons later steps
explanation: The model conditions on its own history; errors compound and propagate.

options: Each verified step resets the multiplication - errors are caught where they happen, not discovered at the end
explanation: Schemas, value checks, test runs: 4.3 applied per iteration.

stem: Auto-raising the budget when it trips causes…
options: Runaway spend with extra steps - escalation must be a human decision
explanation: The wrong response converts one failure into another.

stem: A drift detector firing on 15% of healthy runs should be…
options: Tuned like any classifier - widen the goal set, measure false positives on labelled traces, respond with a nudge not a kill
explanation: Detectors are classifiers over traces; 3.3's precision/recall applies.

stem: Every exit path returns the trace because…
options: Debugging, evals and incident review all consume it - an agent is exactly as debuggable as its trace is complete
